title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page (p.4) of a typed 1965 letter that formulates early versions of what became Grothendieck's 'standard conjectures'. The recipient is addressed with 'tu', probably Serre, though that is not certain.

Notation and setting.
- X is smooth projective of dimension n and Y is a smooth hyperplane section.
- C^i(-) denotes codimension-i cycles modulo 'tau-equivalence', tensored with Q. Tau-equivalence (as in Pic^tau) means that some nonzero multiple is algebraically equivalent to 0, i.e. algebraic equivalence modulo torsion.
- The previous page lists claimed consequences of A and B:
  - the tau-groups are finitely generated;
  - C^m(X) tensor Q_l -> H^{2m}(X)(m) is injective, i.e. homological equivalence implies tau-equivalence;
  - correspondences modulo tau form a semisimple algebra, so motives are semisimple;
  - Galois semisimplicity follows in the Tate conjecture;
  - intermediate 'algebraic' Jacobians behave well.
- Grothendieck calls A and A' 'preliminary' to B. The previous page states the 'suggestive' equivalent form A'': for the affine open U = X - Y, C^i(U) = 0 whenever 2i > n.
- The equivalence with A' comes from the localisation sequence C^{i-1}(Y) -> C^i(X) -> C^i(U) -> 0. So A' must be the Lefschetz/Gysin-type surjectivity of C^{i-1}(Y) -> C^i(X) for 2i > n. That is the cycle analogue of weak Lefschetz, and on the cohomological side corresponds to Artin vanishing H^{2i}(U) = 0 for 2i > n.

What this page says.
1. A'' might hold for every smooth affine variety.
2. More boldly, on every smooth variety (affine or not), a cycle cohomologically equivalent to 0 might be tau-equivalent to 0. For projective X this would follow from A and B.
3. The task now is to invent a procedure to deform a cycle of not-too-large dimension so as to 'push it to infinity', i.e. into the boundary Y. On U such a cycle would then vanish modulo tau, which is a geometric moving-lemma approach to A''.
4. He invites the correspondent to think about it, admitting he started that very day and is writing for lack of an idea.
5. N.B.: H^i is l-adic cohomology with Q_l coefficients, implicitly Tate-twisted by powers of T_l(G_m) tensor Q_l.

The problem served is the programme of proving the Weil conjectures, and building a semisimple category of motives, via Lefschetz-type statements for algebraic cycles.
errors: The hope that, on any smooth variety (in particular any smooth projective one), homological equivalence implies tau-equivalence (algebraic equivalence modulo torsion) is false. Griffiths (1969) gave homologically trivial cycles on quintic threefolds that are not algebraically equivalent to zero even modulo torsion. So the claim 'for projective varieties this would follow from A and B' cannot hold with tau = algebraic equivalence up to torsion, unless the A/B of the letter are themselves false in that form.

Relatedly, the previous page's 'tau-groups are of finite type' (algebraic equivalence modulo torsion) is refuted by Clemens (1983): the Griffiths group can have infinite rank. The published 1969 formulation (Bombay) instead uses homological and numerical equivalence, which corrects this.

The affine version A'' is plausible only modulo algebraic equivalence, not for rational Chow groups. Mumford/Bloch show that CH_0(U) tensor Q is huge for affine opens of surfaces with p_g > 0 (relevant if one were to read C^i as Chow groups).

ideas.what: Lefschetz-type surjectivity for cycles from a hyperplane section (A'), equivalent to the affine vanishing A'': C^i(U) = 0 for 2i > n, U = X - Y
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture / weak Lefschetz for Chow groups modulo algebraic equivalence; cycle analogue of Artin vanishing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1968-69 ('Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles'), Kleiman 1968; Lefschetz-for-Chow questions: Hartshorne 1975, Nori 1993, Paranjape 1994
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures in Grothendieck, Bombay Colloquium 1968 (publ. 1969). The affine formulation A'' is not recalled there; the letter may be in the Grothendieck-Serre correspondence (unsure).

ideas.what: Homological equivalence implies algebraic equivalence modulo torsion on every smooth variety
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of the Griffiths group (tensor Q) - false in general
ideas.where_published: Published version uses numerical equivalence instead

ideas.what: Strategy: deform low-dimensional cycles on an affine variety and push them to infinity
ideas.modern_name: Moving lemmas / connectivity for cycles (Nori connectivity, Paranjape's cycle-theoretic connectivity, Esnault-Levine-Viehweg for low-degree varieties)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposed attacking the Lefschetz standard conjecture through an affine reformulation: cycles of dimension < n/2 on a smooth affine variety are algebraically trivial modulo torsion. He suggested proving it by a moving procedure that pushes cycles to the boundary. Whether the algebraic-equivalence version (on U, or on arbitrary smooth affine varieties) is true or false seems not to be systematically addressed. Griffiths cycles on X restricted to U = X - Y could provide test cases, linked to Nori's connectivity theorem.
missed.quote: Ce qu'il faut pour le moment, c'est inventer un procédé pour déformer un cycle de dimension pas trop grande, pour le pousser à l'infini.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an 'affine Artin-vanishing for cycles' modulo algebraic equivalence, a geometric route to the Lefschetz standard conjecture. It connects to Nori/Paranjape connectivity and to Griffiths-group questions on affine varieties, which are rarely framed this way.

deep.surprise_reason: The standard conjectures are well known. Interesting points are the 1965 formulation via algebraic equivalence modulo torsion (later refuted by Griffiths/Clemens) and the affine 'push to infinity' form A'', which is not prominent in the literature. This is mostly historical detail rather than an unrecognised result.
transcription_corrections: Transcription matches the image; the N.B. reads 'T_l(G_m) ⊗_Z Q_l' (typed with handwritten symbols), as transcribed.
